expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt instructs grounding progress claims in actual tool results / evidence (no fabricated status reports)
expectations.evidence: Prompt block: 'Do not report a batch, phase, or the migration as done without pointing to a test run in this session that proves it. If something is unverified, say so in the log and report — never claim success on inference.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt includes a concrete verification method (e.g., run the migrated tests, verify at intervals) replacing the vague 'double check your work'
expectations.evidence: 'Run Vitest on exactly that batch and get it green', a recorded pre-migration Jest baseline in .migration/baseline.json, and 'Periodically (every ~5 batches) run the full Vitest suite over everything migrated so far.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt addresses autonomous operation: proceed without asking, don't end turn on a promise or unfulfilled intent
expectations.evidence: 'asking "Should I…?" or "Want me to…?" blocks the work — never ask; decide and proceed, recording notable decisions in your run log. End your turn only when the migration is complete or you are blocked on something only a human can provide.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt defines when stopping/flagging IS appropriate (blocked, irreversible action) rather than pure barrel-through
expectations.evidence: 'blocked on something only a human can provide'; quarantine protocol after 3 distinct failed fixes; 'If more than 20% of files end up quarantined, stop converting... make the report's top line say the migration is partial and why'; 'Never touch CI/CD publish or deploy configuration.'

expectations.text: The vacuous 'You MUST NOT make mistakes' instruction is removed or replaced with actionable behavior
expectations.evidence: Phrase absent from the enhanced prompt; notes state: '"You MUST NOT make mistakes" — unactionable and counterproductive... replaced with the thing that actually prevents mistakes: a concrete verification loop... and a rule against claiming success without evidence.'

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining the reasoning behind changes
expectations.evidence: '## Notes on the changes' with 'What was removed and why' and 'Key additions, and the reasoning' sections, e.g. 'without a recorded baseline, the agent can't distinguish its regressions from pre-existing failures.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The fenced enhanced-prompt block (lines 5-124) contains no model or vendor names. Model references ('Recent Claude models', 'Claude API', 'Opus 4.7+') appear only in the commentary/operational notes outside the prompt block.

claims.evidence: Stated in the migration mapping table; consistent with known Jest/Vitest differences but not verifiable from the run outputs.

claims.claim: Grounded progress claims 'nearly eliminates fabricated status reports on long runs'
claims.evidence: Asserted in the notes without evidence; plausible but an unverified effectiveness claim.

claims.claim: output_config.task_budget (beta) exists on the Claude API
claims.evidence: Operational suggestion outside the prompt; cannot be verified from available materials.

suggestions.assertion: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
suggestions.reason: This run names Claude/Opus models in the surrounding commentary while keeping the prompt block clean, and passes. If the intent is vendor-neutral advice overall (not just inside the block), the assertion should say so; otherwise it may under-detect vendor lock-in in delivered guidance.

This run used ~320k tokens vs ~27k for the with_skill run to produce a much longer, highly prescriptive prompt. No assertion penalizes over-prescription or bloat, which is arguably the exact failure mode a prompt-enhancer skill should prevent; consider an assertion bounding prompt length or requiring judgment-based rather than exhaustive step-by-step instructions.

eval_feedback.overall: Both runs pass 7/7; the assertions check presence of good practices but not concision or restraint, so they cannot distinguish the skill's leaner output from the baseline's exhaustive one.
